knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=A matrix containing a column named "mz" with mass information and quantitative intensity columns ;; transformation=A data frame defining biochemical transformations with columns "mass", "group", "formula", and "rt" ;; var=Character vector specifying which columns of the transformation data frame to write as additional character adjacency matrices ;; ppm=Parts-per-million mass tolerance for matching transformations ;; directed=Logical indicating whether to construct a directed structural graph ;; am=An AdjacencyMatrix object ;; model=Character vector specifying statistical models to use (e.g., "pearson", "spearman", "lasso", "randomForest", "clr", "aracne", "bayes", "ggm") ;; type=Method for thresholding/consensus creation ("threshold", "top1", "top2", "mean") ;; args=A list containing filtering criteria (e.g., list(filter = "...") or list(n = 100))
- alternatives: MetaNetter (a Cytoscape plugin) is mentioned as an alternative for network inference based on molecular weight differences and correlation. Upstream peak-picking and preprocessing are typically performed using the xcms/CAMERA suite.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have untargeted high-resolution mass spectrometry data (m/z, retention times, and intensity values) and want to putatively link features to guide metabolite annotation and explore metabolic network topologies.
- pitfalls: MetNet does not perform data normalization, filtering, or isotope removal automatically; users must properly preprocess the input data (e.g., log2/vsn transformation, noise filtering, isotope removal) beforehand. Failing to apply rtCorrection can lead to false-positive structural links if retention time shifts do not match the expected biochemical transformations.

workflows.name: metabolic_network_inference
workflows.intent: Infer a consensus metabolic network topology by combining structural transformations, retention time constraints, spectral similarity, and statistical associations.
input: user_features.csv (matrix of m/z, retention time, and intensity values across samples)
user_transformations.csv (data frame of biochemical transformations with mass, formula, group, and expected rt shift)
workflows.stages:
1. Load and format quantitative and structural metabolomics data.
2. Define biochemical transformations and compute structural adjacency using structural().
3. Refine structural adjacency with retention time constraints using rtCorrection().
4. Integrate MS2 spectral similarity using addSpectralSimilarity() and threshold it.
5. Compute statistical associations across samples using statistical().
6. Threshold statistical adjacency matrices to create a consensus matrix using threshold().
7. Combine structural and statistical networks using combine().
8. Convert to igraph or data frame for downstream visualization and analysis.
workflows.code:
library(MetNet)
data("x_test", package = "MetNet")
x_test <- as.matrix(x_test)
transformations <- data.frame(
    group = transformations[, 1],
    formula = transformations[, 2],
    mass = as.numeric(transformations[, 3]),
    rt = transformations[, 4])
struct_adj <- structural(x = x_test, transformation = transformations, 
    var = c("group", "formula", "mass"), ppm = 10)
struct_adj_dir <- structural(x = x_test, transformation = transformations, 
    var = c("group", "formula", "mass"), ppm = 10, directed = TRUE)
struct_adj <- rtCorrection(am = struct_adj, x = x_test, 
    transformation = transformations, var = "group")
struct_df <- as.data.frame(struct_adj)
struct_df <- struct_df[struct_df$binary == 1, ]
mz_sum <- mz_summary(struct_adj, var = "group")
mz_vis(mz_sum, var = "group")
library(MsCoreUtils)
library(Spectra)
f <- system.file("spectra_matrix/ms2_test.RDS", package = "MetNet")
sps_sub <- readRDS(f)
adj_spec <- Spectra::compareSpectra(sps_sub, FUN = ndotproduct)
colnames(adj_spec) <- sps_sub$id
rownames(adj_spec) <- sps_sub$id
spect_adj <- addSpectralSimilarity(am_structural = struct_adj, 
    ms2_similarity = list("ndotproduct" = adj_spec))
args_thr <- list(filter = "ndotproduct > 0.1 | binary == 1 & is.na(ndotproduct)")
spect_adj_thr <- threshold(am = spect_adj, type = "threshold", 
    args = args_thr)
x_int <- x_test[, 3:ncol(x_test)] |>
    as.matrix()
stat_adj <- statistical(x_int, model = c("pearson", "spearman"))
stat_adj_thr <- threshold(am = stat_adj, type = "threshold", 
    args = args_thr)
args_top <- list(n = 100)
stat_adj_mean <- threshold(am = stat_adj, type = "mean", 
    args = args_top)
comb_adj <- combine(am_structural = struct_adj, am_statistical = stat_adj_mean)
comb_spect_adj <- combine(am_structural = spect_adj_thr, 
                          am_statistical = stat_adj_mean)
adj <- assay(comb_adj, "combine_binary")
diag(adj) <- 1
g <- igraph::graph_from_adjacency_matrix(adj, mode = "undirected", diag = FALSE)
plot(g, edge.width = 2, vertex.label.cex = 0.5, edge.color = "grey")
